title: Equal, no high or low (section 23)
hookLine: this truth is level; there is nothing high or low in it

cards: A carpenter sets a spirit level on a new shelf. The little bubble drifts, wobbles, and settles dead center between the two lines. Level.
Nothing sloping toward one end, nothing tipping the other way. Section twenty-three of the Diamond Sutra uses a word a carpenter would understand.
It says the truth it has been circling is level, even, and then says what that means for anyone who walks on it.

teach.b: First, the word. This teaching is equal, the Buddha tells Subhuti, and there is nothing high or low in it; that is what is called the highest, most complete awakening.
The Sanskrit word for equal is sama: same, even, level. Second, the paradox. The awakening the sutra keeps calling highest has no high and no low inside it.
It's highest precisely because it isn't a ladder, with no top rung for someone to stand on while others wait below. Third, how it's reached.

Without the idea of a self, a person, a being, or a life-span, by doing all good things, one awakens. Those four ideas have come up again and again in this sutra; here they're named again as what has to fall away.
It doesn't say do nothing. It says do all good things, without building a self on top of them. Fourth, the last twist.
These good things, the Buddha adds, are called by the Tathagata not good things; that is why they are called good things.
Even goodness isn't allowed to become a rank.

The moment good deeds become a way of standing above someone, they've stopped being level. In ordinary life we live inside heights: job titles, seating charts, who speaks first at the table, who gets thanked by name.
The sutra doesn't pretend those disappear. It says that underneath them, in what's truest, there's nothing to climb.

how: Mahayana teachers read section 23 as saying awakening holds no ranks: good deeds are done without the ideas of self, person, being or life-span, and without making goodness a way to stand higher.

games.why: the teaching is equal, nothing high or low; even good things are called not good things, so they can't become a rank.

practice: Bring to mind one person you tend to place above you, someone you defer to, and rest with them a moment, breathing, letting the gap level out.
Then bring to mind someone you tend to place below you, maybe without meaning to, someone whose name you don't know or whose opinion you skip past, and let that gap level out too.
Two people, one even ground; breathe with both of them there.

wordCard.voice: Equal. Section twenty-three says this teaching is level, with nothing high or low in it, and that is called the highest awakening. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit and Pali: equal, even, level; section 23 calls the teaching equal.

carryVoice: Your line: no high, no low. The ground is even all the way across. Until tomorrow.
